title: Publish livefs-only arches as they complete
commit_message: Publish livefs-only arches as they complete

diff --git a/incremental-livefs.md b/incremental-livefs.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..1c70511
--- /dev/null
+++ b/incremental-livefs.md
@@ -0,0 +1,138 @@
+# Incremental LiveFS Publication Notes
+
+## Current behaviour
+
+`build-image-set --live` starts live filesystem builds for all configured
+architectures, then waits for every architecture to reach a terminal Launchpad
+state before continuing.
+
+The relevant flow is:
+
+- `run_live_builds(config)` requests all Launchpad builds.
+- It polls until all pending builds have completed or failed.
+- It returns only the successful builds.
+- `build_image_set_locked` then downloads artifacts, builds/copies images, and
+  publishes using the reduced successful architecture set.
+
+For livefs-only products this means a fast architecture cannot be published
+until the slowest architecture has finished building.
+
+## Possible change
+
+The least risky useful change would be limited to livefs-only image paths:
+
+- Start all Launchpad livefs builds as today.
+- Poll them as a set.
+- As each architecture succeeds, download/copy/publish that architecture.
+- Leave debian-cd paths on the existing wait-for-all behaviour.
+
+This should follow the technical boundary rather than a series-specific one:
+
+- Use the incremental path for `is_live_fs_only(config)` builds.
+- Keep the existing path for builds that still require debian-cd.
+
+## Avoid mutable config narrowing
+
+Temporarily mutating `config["ARCHES"]` or `config["CPUARCHES"]` to make helper
+functions process one architecture would be fragile.  `Config` is shared across
+the build and many functions read `config.arches` dynamically.
+
+Prefer passing explicit architecture lists through relevant functions, e.g.:
+
+```python
+download_live_filesystems(config, builds, arches=None)
+build_livecd_base(config, builds, arches=None)
+copy_netboot_tarballs(config, arches=None)
+run_debian_cd(config, apt_state_mgr, arches=None)
+Publisher.publish(date, arches=None)
+```
+
+For debian-cd, if ever needed, `run_debian_cd` can construct a scoped child
+environment with narrowed `ARCHES` and `CPUARCHES` without mutating `config`.
+
+## Existing publication semantics
+
+The publisher already supports mixed-date publication state.
+
+`pending` is normally a symlink to a date directory:
+
+```text
+pending -> YYYYMMDD
+```
+
+When creating a new date directory, `new_publish_dir(date)` hardlinks files from
+the previous `pending` or `current` tree.  This allows single-architecture
+rebuilds to carry over other architectures.
+
+`current` can be either:
+
+- a symlink to one date directory, when all current images come from that date;
+- a real directory containing relative symlinks to files in different date
+  directories, when current images differ by architecture.
+
+Example mixed `current`:
+
+```text
+current/
+  resolute-live-amd64.iso -> ../20260621/resolute-live-amd64.iso
+  resolute-live-arm64.iso -> ../20260620/resolute-live-arm64.iso
+```
+
+## Main semantic concern
+
+Today, mixed-date `pending` mostly happens for exceptional or intentional cases:
+
+- single-architecture rebuilds;
+- partial failures;
+- manually constrained `ARCHES`;
+- interrupted or retried publication.
+
+With incremental per-architecture publication, mixed-date `pending` would become
+the normal transient state for every multi-architecture build.
+
+For example, after the first architecture completes:
+
+```text
+pending -> 20260621
+20260621/resolute-live-amd64.iso    new
+20260621/resolute-live-arm64.iso    carried over from previous pending/current
+20260621/resolute-live-ppc64el.iso  carried over from previous pending/current
+```
+
+Later architectures would replace their carried-over files as they complete.
+
+This fits the existing publication machinery, but changes the practical meaning
+of `pending` during normal builds.  Consumers that currently assume `pending`
+represents a complete build-date candidate set may observe mixed freshness.
+
+## Alternative compromise
+
+If public early availability is not required, a safer compromise is:
+
+- process each architecture internally as soon as its livefs succeeds;
+- download and prepare artifacts incrementally;
+- defer updating `pending` until all architectures are terminal, or until an
+  explicit partial-publication policy applies.
+
+This reduces the post-livefs critical path without making mixed-date `pending`
+normal during successful builds.
+
+## Open questions
+
+- Is `pending` intended to mean latest available per-architecture artifacts, or
+  a complete build-date candidate set?
+- Are consumers prepared for normal transient mixed-date `pending` trees?
+- Should mirror triggering happen per completed architecture or only once at the
+  end?
+- Would Test Observer submissions be duplicated for carried-over artifacts?
+- Should incremental publication be enabled only by an explicit option or
+  environment variable at first?
+
+## Tentative recommendation
+
+Do not broadly change publication semantics by default.
+
+If this is pursued, start with an explicit opt-in mode for livefs-only builds,
+pass architectures explicitly through Python functions, and either defer the
+public `pending` update or deliberately document that `pending` may be mixed
+during normal incremental builds.
